'''Ichinomiya Gozen Shrine''' (一之御前神社) is a shrine located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}, {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|qid=Q11751|lt=Nagoya|1=Nagoya}}, {{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|en|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|qid=Q1355625|lt=Atsuta Ward|1=Atsuta-ku, Nagoya}}. It is one of the {{ill|Keidai-Sessha|ja|Keidai-Sessha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keidai-Sessha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|en|Atsuta Shrine|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine|1=Atsuta Shrine}}.

==Overview==
The founding is said to have occurred either during the era of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō Emperor|1=Emperor Keikō}} or during the reign of {{ill|Tenmu Emperor|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmu Emperor|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q335181}} {{#tag:ref|"‘The palace of the Sun (Emperor Keikō) and the establishment of a separately enshrined Aramitama deity’ (from "Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Compilation of Origins": page 139)"|group="Note"}}. It is located to the northwest of the main shrine, at the far end of the pilgrimage path known as "Kokoro no Komichi", and was relocated to its present site in {{ill|1893|en|1893|qid=Q7840|lt=1893|1=1893}} (Meiji 26); prior to that, it stood near the southeast of the current main shrine {{#tag:ref|"From the perspective of the former main hall, the direction was still to the northwest. (From "April 1893 Atsuta Shrine Reconstruction and Pre-Meiji Structures Location Estimation Diagram": <ref name="名古屋市史地図">"Nagoya City History Map"</ref>)"|group="Note"}}.

It enshrines '''Amaterasu Omikami Aramitama''' (あまてらすおおかみあらみたま) as its deity<ref name="神宮20"/>. The term “Aramitama” refers to a divine spirit that generates fierce, dynamic phenomena and is seen as a symbol of valor and initiative. The reason for its enshrinement at Atsuta Shrine is understood to be equivalent to the existence of {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}’s {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri Shrine}} <small>({{Coord|34|27|22|N|136|43|30|E|scale:2500}})</small><ref name="神宮20"/>.

Referred to as "‘The First Attendant Deity of the Imperial Court’" {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Shrine Official Enshrinement Record' <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒139"/> and 'Atsuta Shrine Record' <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒363">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Compilation of Origins": page 363</ref>, etc."|group="Note"}}, the shrine not only shares an extremely close relationship with the main shrine but also gives the impression of a loyal, trusted aide. During the main shrine’s rituals, it was long customary to first present offerings here—a practice said to carry the meaning of "oni-gui" (poison tasting) {{#tag:ref|"‘When enshrining the main shrine, offerings are first prepared at Aramisaki, as is commonly said to be 'oni-gui’" (from "Oshu Shrine Secret Tradition": <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一7">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 7</ref>)"|group="Note"}}.
<br/>From this, an alternative theory has long existed proposing that, either as a different deity or as a supplementary spirit, {{ill|Ootomo Takehito no Mikoto|ja|大伴武日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ootomo Takehito no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was enshrined. While {{ill|Amano Nobukage|ja|天野信景|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amano Nobukage|1=Amano Sadakage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6535030}} and {{ill|Fukada Masakazu|ja|深田正韶|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukada Masakazu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} support this theory, {{ill|Tsuda Masao|ja|津田正生|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuda Masao|1=Tsuda Masanari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22123474}} dismisses it as "inconceivable"<ref name="地名考75">"Owari Province Place Name Studies": page 75</ref>. According to the "Owari Chronicle", Ootomo Takehito no Mikoto was a warrior who, during Yamato Takeru’s eastern expedition, served as a deputy general on both flanks alongside {{ill|Kibi no Takehiko|lt=Kibi no Takehiko|lt=Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto|ja|吉備武彦命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吉備武彦}} (きびたけひこのみこと) {{#tag:ref|"From the Nihon Shoki (Volume 7, Emperor Keikō)"<ref name="日本書紀上289">"Kazana Nihon Shoki, Volume 1": page 289</ref>|group="Note"}}, and it is said that the placement of this shrine and {{ill|Ryujinja|ja|龍神社 (熱田神宮)|lt=Ryujinja|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryujinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579187|1=Ryujinja}} (whose enshrined deity is Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto) flanking the main shrine like guards originates from this account<ref name="尾張志熱田9">"Owari Chronicle Atsuta": page 9</ref>.
<br/>Before the Edo period, it appears that Ryujinja and this shrine were regarded as a combined entity, and a petition requesting that they be recognized as separate shrines was submitted to the chief priest (dated June 5, 1686 ({{ill|Jōkyō 3|ja|貞享3|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōkyō 3|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579188|1=1686}} April 15))<ref name="神宮史料造営遷宮上412">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Construction and Relocation, Volume I": page 412</ref>{{#tag:ref|"Request stating 'Separate shrines for Ichinomiya and Ryujinja'."|group="Note"}}. This request was granted, and since then, Ichinomiya Gozen Shrine and Ryujinja have existed independently.

As for the origin of the shrine’s name, works such as {{ill|Wahimeimyojoseki|ja|倭姫命世記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wahimeimyojoseki|1=Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q131331326}} note that the character "魂" can be read as "Misaki", giving rise to the theory that it was written as "Ichinomisaki" (一ノ魂) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Main and Subsidiary Shrine Divine Body Sacred Decree Collection Theory'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一34">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 34</ref>|group="Note"}}. Another theory holds that the temporary shrine—where the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|en|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|qid=Q14944|lt=Grass-cutting Sword|1=Kusanagi no Tsurugi}} (also known as the Kusanagi Sword), which was returned to the court in {{ill|686|en|686|qid=Q30619|lt=686|1=686}} (the first year of {{ill|Shuchō|en|Shuchō|qid=Q777413|lt=Shuchō|1=Shuchō}}), was first enshrined—gave the shrine its name<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一184">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 184</ref>. Furthermore, according to the "Owari Chronicle", since the main shrine enshrines five deities—{{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|1=Amaterasu}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}, {{ill|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}}, {{ill|Miyasu-hime no Mikoto|ja|宮簀媛命|lt=Miyasu-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyasu-hime no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Takeinadane no Mikoto|ja|建稲種命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeinadane no Mikoto|1=Takeinadane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486691}}—there is a theory that the name specifically refers to Amaterasu Omikami herself, the foremost of these deities {{#tag:ref|"From 'Owari Chronicle Atsuta': <ref name="尾張志熱田8">page 8</ref> and 'Atsuta Shrine Record': <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒363"/>"|group="Note"}}. It has also been written as "Ichinokami-mae" (一神前) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Shrine Official Enshrinement Record'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒139"/>|group="Note"}}, and as "Ichimusaki" (一御崎) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Main and Subsidiary Shrine Divine Body Sacred Decree Collection'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒171">page 171</ref>|group="Note"}}.
